newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends strong on money mkt rate upswing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends strong on money mkt rate upswing.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed earlier softness to close stronger on Tuesday in the wake of a late surge in secondary money market rates.
"The market went long (on dollars) when the peso reached 7.81 per dollar, then dealers decided to take profits," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed trade 1.4 and 1.6 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7850/7.7870 and 7.7810/7.7840 per dollar.
Overnight Cetes rates climbed 405 basis points to trade at 19.75 percent in late dealing.
Dealers said the peso also owed its late strength to the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, which had gained 11/32 in late trade to yield 6.38 percent, one of its lowest levels this year.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 3.4 centavos weaker at 7.8070/7.8100 per dollar.
